name: Rootd
summary: Anxiety & panic-attack relief app with panic button, breathing exercises, mood journal and guided tools — helps manage panic and anxiety in the moment and over time.
description: Rootd helps individuals cope with panic attacks, acute anxiety, and stress through a simple “panic button” (the Rootr), guided breathing exercises, grounding/visualization tools, sleep aid, mood journaling, and psychoeducational lessons. Available on iOS, Android, and Apple Watch. Free to start, with optional subscription for full access. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search1{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search0{CITATION_END}
patient_summary: Rootd gives you tools to manage panic attacks and anxiety as they happen — a quick-access panic button, calming breathing and visualization exercises, mood tracking and journaling, and resources to ground yourself. Great for sudden panic, chronic anxiety, or stress, but not a replacement for therapy or medical treatment in serious mental health conditions.

metadata.system_requirements: iOS 15.6+ or Android equivalent (varies by device)

linked_conditions.context: Rootd provides tools like an SOS panic button, breathing, grounding, and anxiety-management exercises which may help during panic attacks or acute anxiety episodes. Not intended as standalone treatment.
Techniques like deep breathing, guided visualization, and regular mood tracking may help manage chronic anxiety symptoms, though no formal clinical efficacy data is published.

contraindications: Not a replacement for professional mental-health care or therapy
Not suitable as sole intervention for severe, untreated anxiety disorders or panic disorder with complex comorbidity
May not be sufficient for chronic mental health conditions requiring medical treatment

exclusions: Severe mental illness requiring clinical treatment
Active suicidal ideation, psychosis, or unstable conditions without professional supervision

data_collected: Optional journal / mood entries (local to device or within app, per user consent)
data_shared: Aggregated anonymized analytics (per app store privacy statement) {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search1{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search2{CITATION_END}
No sale of personal data to advertisers (per privacy policy) {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search0{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search3{CITATION_END}

sections.heading: What Rootd Does
sections.text: Rootd offers a panic-attack SOS button (‘Rootr’), guided panic-attack relief via breathing, grounding, visualisations, body-scans and calming sounds. It also includes a mood and anxiety journal for tracking triggers and patterns, sleep aids (white noise, relaxing sounds), psychoeducational lessons about anxiety and panic, and optionally full access via subscription. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search1{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search19{CITATION_END}

sections.heading: Evidence & Limitations
sections.text: Rootd claims to be ‘scientifically validated’ according to its public site, but there is no publicly available peer-reviewed RCT or longitudinal study demonstrating robust efficacy. Experts note Rootd may be useful as a self-help tool or adjunct to therapy for anxiety or panic attacks, but should not be considered a replacement for professional care. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search21{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search19{CITATION_END}

sections.heading: Who Should Use Rootd?
sections.text: Rootd is best for people who:
items: Occasionally experience panic attacks or acute anxiety and need immediate relief
Want tools to ground themselves quickly (breathing, visualization, panic button)
Prefer self-guided support rather than structured therapy
Need an affordable (free-to-start) tool for anxiety relief
Are already receiving therapy and want a supplementary self-help tool
not_recommended: People with chronic or severe anxiety disorders needing clinical treatment
Those expecting Rootd alone to treat or cure anxiety or panic disorder
Users in crisis, with active suicidality or psychosis — should seek professional help instead of relying solely on app

items.description: One-tap button to launch guided panic-attack coping routine — breathing, grounding, calming prompts, and visualizations to help reduce acute anxiety quickly.
items.evidence: Based on CBT and mindfulness-inspired techniques common in anxiety management. Rootd’s design is informed by anxiety-management experts. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search19{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search13{CITATION_END}

items.description: Guided deep-breathing, body-scans, visualization and relaxation audio to calm nervous system during stress, panic, or before sleep.
items.evidence: Breathing and grounding are standard self-help strategies for acute anxiety; Rootd packages them into accessible, on-demand toolsets. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search19{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search6{CITATION_END}

items.description: Users can log moods, triggers, panic attacks, and track patterns or improvements over time — helpful for self-reflection or sharing with a therapist.
items.evidence: Mood & symptom tracking is widely used as part of self-management in mental health — may increase self-awareness and complement other treatments. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search9{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search20{CITATION_END}

items.description: White noise, calming sounds, and relaxation audio to support sleep or wind-down when anxiety interferes with rest.
items.evidence: Sound-based relaxation can help with stress and sleep difficulties; Rootd includes these as part of its toolkit. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search4{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search19{CITATION_END}

items.description: Educational modules about anxiety, panic, triggers, and coping strategies — helps users understand their experiences and build long-term resilience.
items.evidence: Psychoeducation is a core component of cognitive-behavioral self-help; incorporating it helps Rootd provide context and empowerment beyond crisis response. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search0{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search12{CITATION_END}

sections.heading: Cost & Subscription
sections.text: Rootd is free to download and provides basic panic-attack relief tools. Full access to content (lessons, full library, additional tools) requires a paid subscription. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search1{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search20{CITATION_END}

faqs.a: Rootd is free to download and offers core panic-attack relief tools — but full access (lessons, full content) requires a subscription. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search1{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search14{CITATION_END}

faqs.q: Can Rootd replace therapy or medication?
faqs.a: No. Rootd is a self-help / wellness tool. It may help with panic attacks or anxiety symptoms, but it should not replace professional mental-health care when needed. Use it as a supplement or coping aid. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search19{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search20{CITATION_END}

faqs.q: Does Rootd help with panic attacks immediately?
faqs.a: Rootd includes a ‘panic button’ (Rootr) that initiates guided breathing, grounding, and calming tools designed to reduce anxiety in the moment — many users find it helpful for acute panic or stress. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search12{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search0{CITATION_END}

editorial.reviewStatement: Rootd app features and functionality reviewed as of December 2025. Publicly available information on app store listings, official website, and expert reviews (MindTools evaluation) considered. No peer-reviewed RCTs identified; app presented as a self-help and coping tool rather than a clinical treatment.
